title: The Associated Press Statement of News Values and Principles — Anonymous Sources, Attribution, Quotations

extracted.subtask_short: Vetting anonymous-source claims for wire publication
extracted.subtask_description: Judging whether information from an anonymous or third-party source meets AP's evidentiary bar before it can be published as a claim, including how it must be attributed, corroborated, and contextualized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part test for anonymous source material
rubrics_metrics.description: Material from anonymous sources may be used only if all three conditions hold: (1) the material is information, not opinion or speculation, and is vital to the news report; (2) the information is not available except under the conditions of anonymity imposed by the source; (3) the source is reliable and in a position to have accurate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-source corroboration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The AP routinely seeks and requires more than one source. Stories should be held while attempts are made to reach additional sources for confirmation or elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rare cases, one source suffices — when the material comes from an authoritative figure providing information so detailed there is no question of its accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source must have direct knowledge of claim's accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Before agreeing to use anonymous material, the reporter should ask how the source knows the information is accurate, ensuring the source has direct knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters may not agree to a source's request that AP not pursue additional comment or information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution must establish source credibility with specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The story must provide attribution that establishes the source's credibility — simply "a source" is not allowed. Be as descriptive as possible (e.g., "according to top White House aides," "a senior official in the British Foreign Office").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A source's description must never be altered without consulting the reporter. Do not attribute information to anonymous sources when it is obvious or well known — state it as fact instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story must explain reason and motive for anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: The story must explain why the source requested anonymity, and, when relevant, the source's motive for disclosing the information. If a story hinges on documents rather than interviews, the reporter must describe how the documents were obtained, to the extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution ground rules: on/off record, background, deep background
rubrics_metrics.description: On the record: information usable with no caveats, quoting the source by name. Off the record: information that cannot be used for publication at all. Background: information publishable only under conditions negotiated with the source — generally without the source's name, but with an agreed description of their position. Deep background: information usable but without any attribution — the source doesn't want to be identified even anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP reporters should push back on group background briefings and try to move them on the record. Information obtained under any of these can still be pursued with other sources for placement on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party pickups require heightened scrutiny and own-source confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports from other news organizations based on anonymous sources require the most careful scrutiny before being used in AP's own report. The same three-part rule applies: material must be factual and obtainable no other way; the story must be truly significant and newsworthy; use must be authorized by a manager; the story must be balanced and comment must be sought. Before picking up such a story, AP must make a bona fide effort to get it on the record or, at minimum, confirm it through AP's own sources — and should not hesitate to hold the story if there are doubts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If used, source material must be attributed to the originating outlet, including that outlet's own description of its sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations must not be taken out of context; provide setting
rubrics_metrics.description: The same care used to ensure quotes are accurate should ensure quotes are not taken out of context. Quotations are never altered, even to fix grammar. If a quote is too murky to paraphrase accurately, it should not be used. Stories should provide the setting in which a quotation was obtained (press conference, phone interview, hallway conversation) since that context bears on how the claim should be weighed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek response from subject as a fairness/corroboration step
rubrics_metrics.description: AP must make significant efforts to reach anyone portrayed negatively in a story, and give them reasonable time to respond before moving the story; if the parties involved cannot be reached, the story must explain what efforts were made to reach them.
